title: Canonical derived etale inverse-image composition is monoidal
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $u:Y\to X$ and $v:Z\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use small representatives of the small etale sites [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], constant-coefficient module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Inverse image $u^{-1}$ is the termwise descent of the exact module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $\gamma_{u,v}:(uv)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}v^{-1}u^{-1}$ be the termwise-descended inverse of the canonical module composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], normalized by the composite-adjunction unit. For each morphism $w$, write
$$\delta^w_{M,N}:w^{-1}(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}M\otimes^L_\Lambda w^{-1}N$$
for the inverse of the canonical comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], where $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ is the derived tensor product of [def-kun-derived-tensor], and write $\epsilon_w:w^{-1}\underline\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline\Lambda$ for the canonical constant-sheaf comparison [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Then, for all $M,N\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$,
$$
\delta^v_{u^{-1}M,u^{-1}N}\circ v^{-1}(\delta^u_{M,N})\circ\gamma_{u,v,M\otimes^L N}
=(\gamma_{u,v,M}\otimes^L\gamma_{u,v,N})\circ\delta^{uv}_{M,N}.
$$
The same comparison respects the unit: $\epsilon_v\circ v^{-1}(\epsilon_u)\circ\gamma_{u,v,\underline\Lambda}=\epsilon_{uv}$. For every morphism of schemes $w:V\to V'$ and $M\in D(V'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, with $l$ and $r$ the left and right unit constraints of [lem-kun-tensor-unit],
$$w^{-1}(l_M)=l_{w^{-1}M}\circ(\epsilon_w\otimes^L1)\circ\delta^w_{\underline\Lambda,M},\qquad w^{-1}(r_M)=r_{w^{-1}M}\circ(1\otimes^L\epsilon_w)\circ\delta^w_{M,\underline\Lambda}.$$
For a third morphism $t:T\to Z$, the composition comparisons satisfy
$$t^{-1}\gamma_{u,v}\circ\gamma_{uv,t}=(\gamma_{v,t}u^{-1})\circ\gamma_{u,vt}.$$
All equations use the canonical functor associativity and identity identifications and are natural in the derived objects.

proof.text: Use the already proved source-library tensor-composition equation leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison_comp, with g1=v, g2=u and g12=v composed with u. Reverse that equality and rewrite leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso_hom. The helper derivedPullbackCompositionTensor performs this conversion at a general coefficient category, using derivedTensor and curriedTensor_obj_obj, before specializing to ModuleCat Lambda. This proves the first conjunct without repeating the K-flat descent argument already present in the source-library theorem.

Apply leftDerivedUpperStarComp_hom_app_unit to v and u. Rewrite the three oplax unit comparisons using leftDerivedUpperStarOplaxMonoidal_eta (the declaration whose suffix is the Greek eta). This gives exactly the constant-unit composition equation for leftDerivedUpperStarUnitIso.

For each w and K, reverse leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison_leftUnitor_hom and leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison_rightUnitor_hom. Rewrite the tensor comparison as leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso_hom, tensoring with the identity as whiskering, and derivedTensorLeftUnitor or derivedTensorRightUnitor as the respective monoidal unitor. These are precisely the third and fourth conjuncts.

For the final conjunct apply the already proved component associativity theorem leftDerivedUpperStarComp_assoc'_app to t, v, u, the composites t composed with v and v composed with u, and t composed with v composed with u. The composite equalities are reflexivity or category associativity. Assemble these five equations using conjunction introduction. All component maps are those in the unchanged statement; no new choice or alternative comparison is introduced.

The coefficients are the constant Lambda-module etale sheaves and the unbounded D; no base-change morphism appears and no categories are silently identified. The route is fine: the cited units sk-prop-sf-kunneth-ordinary, sk-thm-p1, sk-def-exchange, sk-thm-properbasechange and (in the fix) sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point are all in the transitive uses of sk-thm-sf-compatibility, so no tool_uses are needed. There are no new nodes. The only near-duplicates are condensed/pro-etale analogues, which are not the same statement. Steps 1, 3 and 7 are correct. Repaired faults: (1) E5/C4 in steps 2 and 5. Each relied on a description at the level of sections ('on a pure tensor x(x)y both composites apply c separately'; 'the 07A4 comparison sends the unit tensor to the pulled-back unit tensor') that no cited statement gives. I rewrote both as an injectivity argument. The 03EL comparison is defined through Theta_w(beta)=w_*beta o(eta x eta) of lem-sfb-site-inverse-image-bilinear-adjunction (reviewed). Using the unit normalisation of c_{u,v} and the naturality of d_{u,v}, Theta_u Theta_v of both composites works out to d o phi^flat_{uv} o tau. (2) C4 in step 4: it cited the left unit constraint for an equation that contains no tensor. I rewrote it with adjoints under the composite adjunction and constant sections (prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (1)). (3) Step 6 left the coherence of the d maps and the uniqueness of the threefold comparison implicit. I wrote them out using uniqueness of fibre-product isomorphisms (def-pc-fibre-product), the pasted unit (lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition) and the uniqueness in lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition (2). The corrected item is at fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal.json.
